brief: Morgan Stanley's first "Licence to Scale" report argues environmental constraints, not compute supply, increasingly set the pace and location of AI data centre growth. Power is the most widespread bottleneck: MS chip-sales forecasts imply global DC power demand of 257 GW by 2028 and 378 GW by 2029, while the US faces a 57 GW power shortfall over 2026-28, narrowing to 33 GW after behind-the-meter generation, fuel cells, nuclear co-location and Bitcoin-site conversions. Europe's binding constraint is grid access, with new generation becoming a precondition for connection; APAC is split, with China well-positioned and the rest of Asia needing large investment. These constraints trade off against each other: gas-fired behind-the-meter power eases time-to-power but raises emissions, and water-efficient cooling cuts water use but raises electricity demand. MS's emissions forecast has nearly doubled to 4.5 Gt cumulative over 2026-30. Localised risks (community opposition, moratoriums, water stress, copper tightness) can delay projects, but MS sees no broad threat to long-term growth. MS frames this as investable across power, water, efficiency, decarbonisation and circularity, plus an AI-enabled environmental-tech VC ecosystem as a partial, hard-to-quantify offset to AI's own footprint.
